text:
marta: heads-up — a customer hit a surprise cold-start after we auto-rolled the safetensors bundle; they had pinned a model version but warmup policy still pulled the new shard layout and failed checksum.
ben: oh no. they pinned manifest v1 but our warmup-service honored bundle alias and pulled v2. we should make pin semantics stricter.
owen: agreed. pin should be canonical: pin -> exact bundle-id (immutable). If alias resolves to newer bundle, loader must refuse unless pin_auto_upgrade=true.
ciara: what about private/dedicated pools where ops want auto upgrades? different default per deployment mode maybe.
marta: proposal: manifest pin modes: {alias, bundle_id, bundle_id_with_warmup_opt_in}. default hosted: alias, dedicated/private: bundle_id.
ben: we also need to separate 'serve' pin from 'warmup' pin. Serve can stick to bundle_id but warmup can optionally preload a compatible variant (quantized) if customer allows.
owen: nice. add a compatibility rule: warmup_variant must be declared in manifest with a compatibility fingerprint so runtime can assert kv and tensor layout match.
ciara: to avoid surprise failures, warmup should verify index checksums before mapping. if checksum mismatch, don't map, emit alert, and leave serve using current pinned artifact.
manifest-bot: note: manifest registry reports 3 pinned bundles that differ from alias for tenant: acme-inc.
ben: billing implication: if warmup preloads a larger bundle (e.g., full-fp vs quant), we need to bill warmup_bytes to tenant per policy. ops: add metric warmup_variant_bytes and warmup_variant_id.
ops-bot: logged: adding warmup_variant_bytes to usage API. may take 2 days.
marta: example manifest flags sketch:

```
model_manifest:
  id: my-model
  serve_pin: bundle-20260310-abc123  # exact id -> immutable
  warmup_pin:
    mode: alias | bundle_id | bundle_id_with_optin
    allowed_variants:
      - quant-8
      - int4-xy
    compatibility_fips: ["kv-v1", "tensor-layout-v2"]
```

ciara: loader behavior: if serve_pin is bundle_id, only serve and map that exact bundle. warmup only runs if warmup_pin allows variants and compatibility checks pass.
ownen: add a safe fallback: if warmup fails checksum repeatedly (N times) within T window, disable auto-warmup for that tenant and notify SE. prevents noisy loops.
ben: also, consider a "warmup_debt" ledger: track bytes warmup-ed vs budget. if tenant exceeds warmup_budget for pool, downgrade their warmups to incremental until debt decays.
manifest-bot: audit: warmup_debt currently not tracked per-tenant.
ciara: implement warmup_debt as a leaky-bucket: credit decays over 24h. emergency_override tokens can bypass but are billable.
ops-bot: pre-req: need per-tenant metrics in pool-level allocator - I'll add tenant tags to the mem tracker.
marta: rollout plan: 1) implement strict serve_pin enforcement in loader (opt-in flag) 2) add warmup_pin parsing + compatibility checks 3) instrument warmup_debt + billing 4) soft-rollout by tenant flag, monitor warmup_denied_count and p99.
ownen: tests: attempt warmup of mismatched bundle (simulate checksum drift) and assert serve continues on pinned bundle. also test variant fallback path.
ben: doc update for manifest schema needed. storage team must support returning compatibility_fips at upload time.
ciara: edgecase: tenant pins to bundle that was later GC'd by storage — loader should return 404-like error and ops should provide a repair path. don't auto-redirect to alias.
marta: agreed. sticky pin must be durable or fail loudly.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: warmup-service/pr-7891 created with flag "strict_serve_pin" default=false.
ownen: I'll review the PR and wire the canary. plan to enable for <5% tenants first.
ciara: I'll draft the manifest spec doc and update console UI to show serve_pin vs warmup_pin differences.
ben: thanks team. follow-up: add an RFC-lite for standardizing "variant compatibility fingerprints" so model infra and storage agree.
marta: noted. closing thread.
